title: Invertible sheaves trivialize over inverse images of neighborhoods under finite morphisms
statement: Let $p:Y\to Z$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For every point $z\in Z$ there exists an open neighborhood $V\subseteq Z$ of $z$ such that $M|_{p^{-1}V}\cong\mathcal O_Y|_{p^{-1}V}$ as sheaves of $\mathcal O_Y|_{p^{-1}V}$-modules.

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $U\subseteq Z$ of $z$, and put $X=p^{-1}(U)$ and $L=M|_X$. By the definition of a finite morphism, $X$ is affine. The restricted map $q:X\to U$ is finite: each affine open of $U$ is also an affine open of $Z$ and has the same inverse image and finite map of section rings. Restriction of the local rank-one trivializations of $M$ makes $L$ invertible. It suffices to find the required neighbourhood inside $U$, since $U$ is open in $Z$.

Apply the finite-fibre clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] to $q$ and $z$. Thus $E=q^{-1}(\{z\})$ is finite. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-invertible-finite-set-section] to the affine scheme $X$, the invertible module $L$, and this $E$, obtaining $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ whose image in $L_x/\mathfrak m_xL_x$ is nonzero for every $x\in E$. No closedness of these points is needed.

By [lem-weil-pbc-nonvanishing-section-trivializes], the locus $W=X_s=\{x\in X:s_x\notin\mathfrak m_xL_x\}$ is open and multiplication by $s$ gives an isomorphism $\mathcal O_W\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_W$. Step 2 gives $E\subseteq W$. Set $C=X\setminus W$, a closed subset of $X$.

The closed-map clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres] says that $q(C)$ is closed in $U$. Put $V=U\setminus q(C)$. If $z$ belonged to $q(C)$, there would be $x\in C$ with $q(x)=z$, contradicting $q^{-1}(\{z\})\subseteq W$. Hence $z\in V$. Moreover, if $x\in q^{-1}(V)$ belonged to $C$, then $q(x)\in q(C)$, contradicting $q(x)\in V$. Thus $q^{-1}(V)\subseteq W$.

Restrict the isomorphism $\mathcal O_W\xrightarrow{\sim}L|_W$ and its inverse to the open $q^{-1}(V)$. Their compositions remain identities under restriction, so they give the required trivialization. Since $V\subseteq U$ and $U$ is open in $Z$, the set $V$ is an open neighbourhood of $z$ in $Z$, $q^{-1}(V)=p^{-1}(V)$, and $L|_{q^{-1}(V)}=M|_{p^{-1}(V)}$. This also handles an empty fibre: step 2 permits $E=\varnothing$, and the same complement-of-image argument applies.

Step 1 (elementary): restrict to an affine U, using that def-weil-finite-integral-morphism makes the inverse image affine and the restriction finite. Step 2: the fibre is finite by clause 2 of the Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres (finite_preimage_singleton), and the new node gives s nonvanishing on that fibre. Steps 4-5 (elementary): finite maps are closed, so V=U minus q(X minus W) is a neighbourhood of z with q^-1 V inside W, and restricting the isomorphism to it gives the trivialization.
